title: Short Encoding of Words
hints: 'word A is a suffix of word B' is the same as 'reverse(A) is a prefix of reverse(B)' - reversing turns a suffix relationship into a familiar prefix relationship
reverse every word, and insert all the reversed words into a trie

after inserting everything, a word needs to be KEPT only if its reversed form ends at a leaf node (a node with no children) - if it has children, some other longer word's reversal passes through it, meaning the original word is a suffix of that other word and can be dropped
sum (word length + 1) over exactly the kept words - the '+1' accounts for the '#' separator after each one
watch out for duplicate words: insert them as normal, but only count a given distinct word once toward the final sum, even if it appears multiple times in the input list
commonMistakes: checking prefixes instead of suffixes (forgetting to reverse the words first)
double-counting duplicate words in the final length sum

using 'is a leaf' incorrectly - a node can be both end-of-word AND have children if one word's reversal is itself a proper prefix of another's; only leaf nodes (no children at all) correspond to words that must be kept

content.problemStatement:
You're given a space-delimited string of lowercase words. You want to
build a single "reference string" made of some of these words joined by
'#' characters (with a trailing '#'), such that every word in the list
appears as a suffix of the reference string ending right before one of
those '#' markers.

**Return the minimum possible length of such a reference string.**

A word can be dropped from the reference string entirely if it is already a suffix of some other included word, since that word's encoding already covers it.
constraints: words consist only of lowercase English letters, separated by single spaces
notes: duplicate words in the list (only counted once toward the final length)
a word that is a suffix of another word but shares no prefix with it, e.g. 'bell' and 'ell'
no word is a suffix of any other word (every word must be kept)

sampleTestCases.explanation: "me" is a suffix of "time", so it can be dropped; the reference string is "time#bell#" (4+1 + 4+1 = 10)
"time" is a suffix of both "atime" and "botime", so it is dropped; reference string covers "atime#botime#" (5+1 + 6+1 = 13)
"bc" is a suffix of "abc", and "c" is a suffix of "abc" too, so only "abc" is needed: "abc#" (3+1 = 4)

optimal.time: O(total characters) to build the trie and check every word
optimal.pattern: reverse every word and insert the reversed strings into a trie; a word can be dropped exactly when its reversed form is a strict prefix of some other reversed word's path in the trie, which is equivalent to that word's trie node NOT being a leaf (having at least one child)

bruteForce.approach: dedupe the words, then for each word check whether it is a suffix of any OTHER word in the list; keep only the words that are not a suffix of anything else, and sum (length + 1) over the kept words
bruteForce.time: O(n^2 * m) checking every pair for the suffix relationship
